# Exponential parameter floor and scale-resolved logarithmic defects

This uses precisely the actual separator hypotheses of
`candidate 3432196fb93eb580`. It gives a
pointwise prelimit floor and refines that note's defect inequality by
retaining the exponential scale of concentration. It does not exclude
defects or prove the OC numerical bound.

## 1. Standing hypotheses and a pointwise floor

Keep the compact normal/physical space, actual sampled boundary measures
eta_j, positive finite-PL concave parameters L_j, and the SAME cap loads
0<=W_j<=1. Write

    ell_j=-log L_j,
    Xi_j=W_j-beta_j+lambda_j ell_j+R_j,
    |R_j|<=C lambda_j,

where lambda_j>0 tends to zero and beta_j tends to beta. For every globally
finite convex Phi and every continuous nonnegative normal weight psi the
actual separator gives

    integral Xi_j psi Phi d eta_j <= 0.                    (1)

As in the cited note, L_j is positive on a neighborhood of the current
canonical body. Every convex function used below on that neighborhood has
a globally finite convex extension agreeing on the body: take the supremum
of its supporting affine functions based on a slightly larger compact
neighborhood. Their slopes are bounded at each FIXED j. No uniform bound
on those slopes is required by (1).

Put a_j=beta_j/lambda_j+C and use the allowed nonnegative convex test

    Phi_j=(ell_j-a_j)_+.

On its support, W_j>=0 and R_j>=-C lambda_j give

    Xi_j >= lambda_j(ell_j-a_j)=lambda_j Phi_j.

Consequently (1), with psi=1, implies

    0 >= integral Xi_j Phi_j d eta_j
      >= lambda_j integral Phi_j^2 d eta_j >= 0.

Thus Phi_j is zero eta_j-almost everywhere. It is continuous, and the
surface measure of a positive convex fiber has full support on its boundary
(in d=1 this is counting measure on the two endpoints). It is therefore
zero on every sampled boundary. Concavity of L_j extends the lower bound
to the whole sampled fibers and their canonical convex hull. We have proved

    L_j(w) >= exp(-beta_j/lambda_j-C)                     (2)

on that hull. Equivalently, for r_j=lambda_j ell_{j,+},

    0 <= r_j <= max(0,beta_j+C lambda_j).                 (3)

The theorem concerns the positive d-fiber framework of the separator;
it does not purport to replace the separate intrinsic-degeneracy reduction.

## 2. Retain the rate as a coordinate of the defect measure

The existing trace bound gives uniformly bounded masses
integral ell_{j,+} d eta_j. On the product with a common compact rate
interval define

    Bhat_j=ell_{j,+} eta_j delta_(r_j),
    Ahat_j=W_j ell_{j,+} eta_j delta_(r_j).

Pass to a joint subsequence. If L_j converges uniformly to L, eta_j converges
to eta, eta({L=0})=0, and W_j eta_j converges to W eta, exactly the bounded
logarithm argument from the cited note gives

    Bhat_j -> ell_+ eta delta_0 + bhat,
    Ahat_j -> W ell_+ eta delta_0 + ahat,                  (4)

where 0<=ahat<=bhat and the residual measures are supported on
{L=0} times [0,beta]. Let pi forget the rate coordinate. Then

    pi_*bhat=b,   pi_*ahat=a,
    pi_*(r bhat)=q.                                      (5)

The last equality follows by testing the compact rate coordinate, since
r Bhat_j=lambda_j ell_{j,+}^2 eta_j with its rate recorded. The ordinary
part in (4) has rate zero. This proves (5) without a separate uniform
integrability claim for the squared logarithm.

## 3. A family of valid convex perspective tests

Let g:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) be finite, convex and nondecreasing. For
fixed lambda>0 define k(s)=s_+ g(lambda s_+). This k is convex and
nondecreasing. For example, in the smooth positive part,

    k'=g+lambda s g' >=0,
    k''=2lambda g'+lambda^2 s g'' >=0.

Approximation by convex nondecreasing functions, or the same monotone
one-sided derivative calculation, covers nonsmooth g and the corner at
zero. The function

    F(a,b)=a k(log(a/b)-T),  a,b>0,

is jointly convex. Indeed F is the perspective b phi(a/b), where
phi(t)=t k(log t-T) and phi''=(k'+k'')/t>=0 in the distributional sense.
Also F is nondecreasing in a and nonincreasing in b, since its one-sided
derivatives have signs k+k'>=0 and -(a/b)k'<=0.

For any positive globally finite convex f, take T>sup log f on the common
compact range and put c=T-log f>0. Composition with convex f and concave
L_j therefore gives the admissible convex test

    Phi_(j,T)=f (ell_j-c)_+ g(lambda_j(ell_j-c)_+).        (6)

The extension explained in Section 1 makes (6) an actual test in (1).
The same proof applies first to f bounded below by a positive constant
on a neighborhood of the range; nonnegative f follows by f+delta below.

## 4. Limiting the tests without losing the rate

All values of r_j lie in one compact interval by (3). On a slightly larger
interval g is Lipschitz. For fixed T and f the difference between (6) and
f ell_{j,+} g(r_j), after adding

    f min(ell_{j,+},c) g(0),

has absolute value at most a constant times lambda_j ell_{j,+}.
To check this, write s=ell_{j,+}, t=(s-c)_+, so s-t=min(s,c).
Then t[g(lambda_j t)-g(lambda_j s)] is bounded by
Lip(g)lambda_j c s, while
(s-t)[g(lambda_j s)-g(0)] is bounded by the same expression.

Thus its integral tends to zero, also after multiplication by bounded
W_j-beta_j. Using (4), the limit of that part of (1) is

    g(0) integral psi(W-beta) f(ell-c)_+ d eta
       + integral psi f g(r) d(ahat-beta bhat).          (7)

The logarithmic part satisfies

    integral psi lambda_j ell_j Phi_(j,T) d eta_j
       -> integral psi f r g(r) d bhat.                 (8)

For (8), on the support of (6) ell_j>c>0. The bounded rate, bounded c,
and Lipschitz estimate above make the difference from
psi f r_j ell_{j,+} g(r_j) have integral O(lambda_j integral ell_{j,+}).
Its limit follows from (4); the ordinary part has r=0. The R_j term is
bounded by a constant times lambda_j integral ell_{j,+}, and vanishes.

After taking j to infinity, let T tend to infinity in (7). Dominated
convergence applies because ell_+ is eta-integrable. Finally replace f
by f+delta and let delta decrease to zero if necessary. We obtain, for
EVERY nonnegative globally finite convex f, continuous psi>=0, and finite
nonnegative convex nondecreasing g,

    integral psi f g(r) d ahat
      + integral psi f r g(r) d bhat
        <= beta integral psi f g(r) d bhat.             (9)

Taking g=1 recovers the previous a+q<=beta b inequality. Taking
g(r)=(r-t)_+ retains an additional inequality on every upper rate tail;
integer powers g(r)=r^m, m>=1, are also allowed.

For example define measures on the normal/physical space

    b_t=pi_*((r-t)_+ bhat),
    a_t=pi_*((r-t)_+ ahat).

For 0<=t<=beta, (9) implies the precise positive-convex bound

    integral psi f d a_t
      + integral psi f (r-t)_+^2 d bhat
        <= (beta-t) integral psi f d b_t.               (10)

No interval-by-interval disintegration of (9) is claimed. The allowed
rate weights are convex and nondecreasing, and the allowed physical tests
remain nonnegative convex functions. In particular (9) does not imply the
pointwise inequality W+r<=beta for an arbitrary chosen limiting selector.
It controls the retained actual weighted measures. Nor does (2) give a
uniform positive floor as lambda_j tends to zero.
